extracted.intended_audience: TeX users, macro programmers, and implementers (advanced TeX programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference summary of TeX primitive command syntax and the semantic behavior of commands in vertical, horizontal, and math modes — intended to guide writing correct TeX input and macros and understanding engine behavior. Covers assignment forms, box construction, grouping, whatsits, marks, insertions, page builder, and mode-dependent rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: General-text / filler syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: hﬁlleri −→ hoptional spacesi | hﬁlleri\relaxhoptional spacesi; hgeneral texti −→ hﬁlleri{hbalanced textihright bracei
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general text is built from optional spaces and \relax-delimited filler; its main purpose is to specify the balanced text inside the braces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple-assignment forms
rubrics_metrics.description: hsimple assignmenti −→ hvariable assignmenti | harithmetici | hcode assignmenti | hlet assignmenti | hshorthand deﬁnitioni | hfontdef tokeni | hfamily assignmenti | hshape assignmenti | \readhnumberi to hoptional spacesihcontrol sequencei | \setboxh8-bit numberihequalsihﬁllerihboxi | \fonthcontrol sequenceihequalsihﬁle nameihat clausei | hglobal assignmenti
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments appear in a fixed set of patterns; use the appropriate form for integers, dimensions, glue, tokens, arithmetic operations, code/let definitions, font and shape assignments, reads, setbox, and global variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable-assignment categories
rubrics_metrics.description: hvariable assignmenti covers integer, dimen, glue, mu-glue, token, and token-variable assignments (e.g., \countdef, \dimendef, \skipdef, \muskipdef, \toksdef).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each variable assignment form expects a specific quantity type (number/dimen/glue) on the right-hand side; use the matching \...def or parameter register form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic assignment forms
rubrics_metrics.description: harithmetici −→ \advancehinteger variableihoptional byihnumberi | \advancehdimen variableihoptional byihdimeni | \advancehglue variableihoptional byihgluei | \advancehmuglue variableihoptional byihmugluei | \multiplyhnumeric variableihoptional byihnumberi | \dividehnumeric variableihoptional byihnumberi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \advance/\multiply/\divide with proper numeric/dimen/glue/muglue targets; optional 'by' may be omitted (spaces allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric-variable type rules
rubrics_metrics.description: hnumeric variablei −→ hinteger variablei | hdimen variablei | hglue variablei | hmuglue variablei
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric variables for multiply/divide can be an integer, dimen, glue, or mu-glue register; choose appropriate variant for the operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax for token assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: htoken variablei −→ htoken parameteri | htoksdef tokeni | \toksh8-bit numberi; token variables can be assigned general text or token lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Token-register and token-parameter assignments use balanced text; \afterassignment and similar behaviors depend on token placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No expansion scanning for \let and \futurelet
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX does not expand tokens when it scans the arguments of \let and \futurelet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that the meaning of the tokens is preserved; use \expandafter or explicit expansion when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code-assignment and number-range constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: hcode assignmenti −→ hcodenameih8-bit numberihequalsihnumberi; the hnumberi must not be negative except for \delcode; ranges: at most 15 for \catcode, 32768 for \mathcode, 255 for \lccode/\uccode, 32767 for \sfcode, and 224−1 for \delcode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure code numbers fall within allowed ranges for the particular codename to avoid undefined or erroneous behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape-assignment (\parshape) dimension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In a hshape assignmenti with hnumberi = n, the hshape dimensionsi are hemptyi if n ≤ 0, otherwise they consist of 2n consecutive hdimeni.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting \parshape, supply exactly 2n dimension parameters when n>0; zero or negative n yields empty shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping restores non-global assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: All assignments mentioned so far obey TeX's grouping structure: changed quantities are restored when the current group ends, unless the change was global.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \global prefix for assignments that must survive group ends; otherwise local changes are reverted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global assignments that ignore \global prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: hglobal assignmenti −→ hfont assignmenti | hhyphenation assignmenti | hbox size assignmenti | hinteraction mode assignmenti | hintimate assignmenti; for these, presence or absence of \global has no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments that affect global tables (fonts, hyphenation, box sizes, interaction mode, and intimate/site-specific font parameters) are inherently global; \global is irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font-assignment parameter constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When a \fontdimen value is assigned, the hnumberi must be positive and not greater than the number of parameters in the font's metric file, unless that font information has just been loaded into TEX’s memory; then increasing the number of parameters is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assign out-of-range \fontdimen indices; only during initial font load can the parameter count be increased (see Appendix F).

rubrics_metrics.name: File-name conventions and portability
rubrics_metrics.description: A hﬁle namei should consist of hoptional spacesi followed by explicit character tokens (after expansion). A sequence of six or fewer ordinary letters and/or digits followed by a space should be a portable file name. Uppercase letters are not equivalent to lowercase in file names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short, lowercase file names (≤6 letters/digits) followed by a space for maximum portability across systems; ask local system administrators for platform-specific conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of expansion in certain constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX takes precautions so constructions like '\chardef\cs=10\cs' and '\font\cs=name\cs' won't expand the second \cs until the assignments are done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX sequences assignments and later expansions to avoid premature expansion; rely on this when writing macros that refer to registers being defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setbox box-specification and construction behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: hboxi −→ \boxh8-bit numberi | \copyh8-bit numberi | \lastbox | \vsplith8-bit numberi to hdimeni | \hboxhbox speciﬁcationi{hhorizontal mode materiali} | \vboxhbox speciﬁcationi{hvertical mode materiali} | \vtophbox speciﬁcationi{hvertical mode materiali}; \setbox causes TeX to evaluate numeric args, push them on a stack, begin a group, enter restricted horizontal mode (for \hbox), build the box, then restore group and complete \setbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using \setbox with explicit box constructions, TeX executes potentially thousands of commands inside the group while building the box — the box's destined usage does not change how it's built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on \lastbox
rubrics_metrics.description: The \lastbox operation is not permitted in math modes, nor is it allowed in vertical mode when the main vertical list has been entirely contributed to the current page. It is allowed in horizontal modes and in internal vertical mode, where it removes the last hbox or vbox of the current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use \lastbox in math mode or after contribution list was transferred to the page; use only in appropriate modes where the current list still holds the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode-independent commands semantics (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several commands behave the same regardless of mode: \relax (does nothing), '}' (ends group), \begingroup / \endgroup (enter/exit group without changing mode), \showthe (shows internal quantity), \showbox / \show / \showlists (diagnostics), \shipout (send box to DVI), \ignorespaces, \afterassignment, \aftergroup, \uppercase/\lowercase, \message / \errmessage, open/close/read/write primitives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands manipulate grouping, diagnostics, token insertion, case conversion (no expansion), IO, and logging — understand their universal semantics when writing macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: \afterassignment insertion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: \afterassignmenthtokeni: the htokeni is saved and will be inserted back into the input just after the next assignment command is performed. If another \afterassignment occurs before the next assignment, the second overrides the first. If the next assignment is a \setbox and the assigned hboxi is \hbox or \vbox or \vtop, the htokeni will be inserted just after the '{' in the box construction, not after the '}', and before any \everyhbox/\everyvbox tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \afterassignment to schedule a token right after the following assignment; note its special placement with \setbox into constructed boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \aftergroup insertion ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: \aftergrouphtokeni: the htokeni is saved on TeX’s stack and will be inserted after the current group completes and its local assignments are undone. If several \aftergroup commands occur in the same group, they are inserted in the same order they appeared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \aftergroup to append tokens immediately after a group ends; ordering is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case conversion commands behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \uppercasehgeneral texti, \lowercasehgeneral texti: the hbalanced text is converted using the \uccode or \lccode table with no expansion, and then TeX reads that balanced text again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands only alter character codes per code tables without expanding tokens; to affect expansion, combine with other primitives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message and error message semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: \messagehgeneral texti, \errmessagehgeneral texti: balanced text (with expansion) is written to the user terminal in normal or error format; on \errmessage the \errhelp tokens will be shown if nonempty and if the user asks for help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \errmessage for fatal or user-facing error messages and supply \errhelp for interactive troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whatsit recording for deferred IO
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands like \openouth4-bit numberi=filename, \closeouth4-bit numberi, \writehnumberihgeneral texti are recorded into a whatsit item appended to the current list and performed later during any \shipout that applies to the list, unless the list is part of a box inside leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writes and open/close actions may be deferred until shipout; be careful when expecting immediate file output — use \immediate for immediate effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: \special whatsit behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \specialhgeneral texti: the balanced text is expanded and put into a whatsit appended to the current list; it will appear in the DVI as an instruction to subsequent software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \special to embed DVI-level instructions; text is expanded before being stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty and kern items in lists
rubrics_metrics.description: \penaltyhnumberi appends a penalty item; \kernhdimeni and \mkernhmudimeni append kern items carrying specified dimensions. In vertical mode, these denote vertical space; \mkern allowed only in math modes. \penalty also causes TeX to exercise the page builder in vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use penalties and kerns to guide page/line breaking; be mindful of mode-specific interpretations and the page builder triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal primitives (\unpenalty/\unkern/\unskip) restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: \unpenalty, \unkern, \unskip remove the last item on the current list if of the corresponding type; not permitted in vertical mode if the main vertical list has been entirely contributed to the current page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These primitives are safe only while the current list still owns the trailing item; avoid using them when the current page has already been frozen to the output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark items and migration
rubrics_metrics.description: \markhgeneral texti: balanced text is expanded and placed into a mark item appended to the current list; it may become the replacement text for \topmark, \firstmark, \botmark, \splitfirstmark, and/or \splitbotmark if the mark migrates into a vertical list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks placed in horizontal or math lists have effect only after migration into a vertical list; use marks to communicate running headers/footers and split-related marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertions (\insert) and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: \inserth8-bit numberihﬁlleri{hvertical mode materiali}; the h8-bit numberi must not be 255. The '{' causes internal vertical mode and grouping; when '}' is read the vertical list is packaged into an insertion item appended to the current list, using \splittopskip, \splitmaxdepth, and \floatingpenalty that were current in the group. An insertion leads to a page insertion only if it appears in TeX's main vertical list; TeX exercises the page builder after appending an \insert in vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use insertions for footnotes/floats but avoid register 255; remember that insertions only effect pages when they are in the main vertical list and that their split parameters come from the group where they were built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vadjust behavior and migration unwrapping
rubrics_metrics.description: \vadjusthﬁlleri{hvertical mode materiali} is similar to \insert, but not allowed in vertical modes. When an adjustment item migrates from a horizontal list to a vertical list, the vertical list inside the adjustment item is unwrapped and put directly into the enclosing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \vadjust to attach vertical material to the current horizontal list; on migration the material is integrated directly into the vertical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-builder concept in vertical mode
rubrics_metrics.description: In vertical modes TeX periodically takes material from the main vertical list (contribution list) to the current page; whenever TeX tries to empty the contribution list it 'exercises the page builder' and the output routine might be invoked. The contribution list concept exists only in the outermost vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page breaking and output routine invocation are tied to the page builder; avoid surprising side-effects by knowing when the contribution list is being drained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interline glue and \prevdepth initialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Interline glue inserted before boxes is based on \prevdepth, \baselineskip, \lineskip, and \lineskiplimit. \prevdepth is initially set to -1000pt (inhibits interline glue) whenever TeX begins to form a vertical list, except for \halign and \noalign where outer conventions continue inside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track \prevdepth carefully when manipulating vertical lists and alignments; setting it to -1000pt suppresses interline glue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical glue primitives
rubrics_metrics.description: \vskiphgluei, \vfil, \vfill, \vss, \vfilneg append glue items to the current vertical list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vertical glue primitives to control stretch/shrink in vertical lists (pages/boxes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders and rule/box specification
rubrics_metrics.description: hleadersi −→ \leaders | \cleaders | \xleaders; hbox or rulei −→ hboxi | hvertical rulei | hhorizontal rulei; hrule speciﬁcationi may include Width/Height/Depth dimensions. A glue item that produces leaders is appended to the current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders produce repeated boxes/rules across glue; use the appropriate leaders variant for centering/clearing effects and supply correct rule dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space tokens in vertical mode
rubrics_metrics.description: hspace tokeni. Spaces have no eﬀect in vertical modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on literal spaces to produce vertical glue; use explicit \vskip or glue primitives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appending an hbox to vertical list and migration
rubrics_metrics.description: When an hboxi is appended in vertical mode, the vertical list receives (1) interline glue, (2) the new box, and (3) vertical material that migrates out of the new box (if the hboxi was an \hbox command). Then \prevdepth is set to the new box's depth, and TeX exercises the page builder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that horizontal material inside an \hbox can migrate vertical material to the enclosing vertical list when boxes are appended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moveleft / moveright in vertical mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \movelefthdimenihboxi and \moverighthdimenihboxi act exactly like an unadorned hboxi except that the new box appended to the vertical list is shifted left or right by the specified amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moveleft/moveright to horizontally offset boxes being appended to vertical lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: \unvbox / \unvcopy semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: \unvboxh8-bit numberi and \unvcopyh8-bit numberi: if register is void nothing happens; otherwise the register must contain a vbox. The vertical list inside that box is appended to the current vertical list unchanged. \unvbox voids the register; \unvcopy leaves it unchanged. \prevdepth is not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \unvbox to transfer box contents to the current list and free the register; use \unvcopy to peek without destroying the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal rule affects \prevdepth
rubrics_metrics.description: hhorizontal rulei: the specified rule is appended to the current list. Then \prevdepth is set to -1000pt, inhibiting interline glue for the next box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inserting a horizontal rule resets \prevdepth; this influences subsequent interline glue calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: \halign grouping and internal-mode rules
rubrics_metrics.description: \halignhbox speciﬁcationi{halignment materiali}: alignment material involves multiple grouping levels; TeX enters internal vertical mode for \noalign groups and when appending lines; each individual entry is processed in restricted horizontal mode and vboxed; vertical material migrates to the enclosing vertical list; \prevdepth at start/end is handled to compute interline glue correctly. Alignment-token commands (\noalign, \omit, \span, \cr, \crcr, &) are intercepted by alignment and do not get delivered to the stomach unless alignment is lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignments are complex: understand nested mode transitions and the special interception of alignment tokens when writing macros that interact with \halign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands that begin a paragraph in vertical mode (intrinsically horizontal)
rubrics_metrics.description: hhorizontal commandi −→ hletteri | hotherchari | \char | hchardef tokeni | \noboundary | \unhbox | \unhcopy | \valign | \vrule | \hskip | \hfil | \hfill | \hss | \hfilneg | \accent | \discretionary | \- | \  | $; if any of these tokens occurs as a command in vertical mode, TeX performs an \indent automatically, leading to horizontal mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encountering intrinsically horizontal tokens in vertical mode will start a paragraph (enter horizontal mode) and reprocess the token; design macros accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \end and \dump behavior in vertical mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \end is not allowed in internal vertical mode. In regular vertical mode it terminates TeX if the main vertical list is empty and \deadcycles=0; otherwise TeX backs up the \end so it can be read again and exercises the page builder after appending a box/glue/penalty forcing output. \dump (INITEX only) is treated like \end but must not appear inside a group and outputs a format file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \end inside internal vertical mode; \dump is an INITEX-only facility — be careful about grouping when producing formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error recovery for misplaced primitives in vertical/horizontal modes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a primitive inappropriate for the current mode appears, TeX issues an error and tries to recover: for math-related tokens it may insert a '$' to enter math mode; for totally misplaced tokens like \endcsname or \omit or \eqno, TeX reports the error and ignores them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate TeX’s automatic recovery strategies when debugging malformed input; use tracing tools (e.g., \tracingall) for diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space-factor and horizontal-mode initialization
rubrics_metrics.description: In horizontal mode the space factor modifies space widths. \spacefactor is initially set to 1000 when TeX begins a horizontal list (except for \valign and \noalign where the outer value continues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on \spacefactor starting at 1000 for ordinary paragraphs; character commands adjust it via \sfcode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal glue, leaders, and control-space
rubrics_metrics.description: \hskiphgluei, \hfil, \hfill, \hss, \hfilneg append glue to the horizontal list. hleadersihbox or ruleihorizontal skipi appends glue-producing leaders. A control-space (\ ) appends glue equal to the space inserted when \spacefactor=1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use horizontal glue primitives to fine-tune interword/inter-box spacing and leaders for repeated patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hbox and spacefactor reset
rubrics_metrics.description: When an hbox is appended to the horizontal list (constructed or from register), it is appended and \spacefactor is set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes reset the interword space computation; after boxes or rules expect spacefactor-normal behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unhbox / unhcopy semantics in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \unhboxh8-bit numberi and \unhcopyh8-bit numberi: if void nothing happens; otherwise the register must contain an hbox; its horizontal list is appended to the current horizontal list unchanged; \unhbox voids the register, \unhcopy preserves it; \spacefactor is not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \unhbox to inline previously typeset horizontal material; \unhbox removes register contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical commands that terminate paragraphs in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: hvertical commandi −→ \unvbox | \unvcopy | \halign | \hrule | \vskip | \vfil | \vfill | \vss | \vfilneg | \end | \dump: these conclude the current paragraph in unrestricted horizontal mode. In restricted horizontal mode they are forbidden (insert 'par' in regular horizontal mode if seen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In horizontal mode, encountering vertical primitives forces paragraph ending; avoid placing vertical primitives inside restricted horizontal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character sequence processing and \noboundary
rubrics_metrics.description: hletteri, hotherchari, \charh8-bit numberi, hchardef tokeni, \noboundary: successive character commands are processed as a unit for ligatures and kerns, possibly influenced by invisible boundary characters at left and right unless \noboundary appears. Each character adjusts \spacefactor using the \sfcode table; in unrestricted horizontal mode a \discretionary{}{}{} item may be appended after characters whose code is \hyphenchar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character runs are combined per font ligature/kern tables and affect spacefactor; use \noboundary to prevent boundary-character behavior when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: \accent handling and optional assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: \accenth8-bit numberihoptional assignmentsi: optional assignments (zero or more assignment commands other than \setbox) allow the accenter and accentee to be in different fonts; if no following character, \accent acts like \char but sets \spacefactor=1000. Otherwise accent is applied and \spacefactor set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use optional assignments preceding \accent to switch fonts for accenter/accentee; accents influence spacing by resetting spacefactor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italic-correction primitive \/
rubrics_metrics.description: \/ appends an explicit kern for the italic correction of the last character or ligature on the current list (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert \/ where the italic correction of the preceding glyph is required (e.g., before punctuation following italic text).

rubrics_metrics.name: \discretionary operand restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: \discretionaryhgeneral textihgeneral textihgeneral texti: the three general texts are processed in restricted horizontal mode and should contain only fixed-width things (characters, ligatures, kerns, boxes, and rules); they append a discretionary item and do not change \spacefactor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing discretionary material, avoid glue/penalty items etc. inside the discretionary texts to ensure valid break behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math shift ($) rules in horizontal and restricted modes
rubrics_metrics.description: A $ starts math mode or display math mode: TeX looks ahead for a second $ to decide. If it finds $$ in unrestricted horizontal mode, it breaks the current paragraph (unless empty), returns to vertical mode, sets display parameters, enters grouping, inserts \everydisplay, exercises page builder, processes display math, appends display to vertical list, exercises page builder, increases \prevgraf by 3, and resumes horizontal mode with empty list and \spacefactor=1000. Otherwise a single $ starts inline math using \everymath and results in a horizontal inclusion with \spacefactor=1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $ and $$ with care; $$ has extensive side-effects (paragraph break, display math insertion) while inline $ converts following material to a math list embedded in the current horizontal list.

rubrics_metrics.name: General error handling in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: If any other primitive command inappropriate for horizontal mode occurs, an error message is given. For mathematical tokens TeX tries to insert a '$' before the offending token; this will enter math mode. Otherwise TeX reports the error and attempts reasonable recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect TeX to attempt automatic fixes (e.g., inserting '$'); when debugging, inspect the error and the input context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-mode atom and field structure (intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Math lists contain three-pronged "atoms" in thirteen flavors (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner, Over, Under, Acc, Rad, Vcent). Each atom has three fields: nucleus, superscript, subscript; each field can be empty or contain a math symbol, a box, or a subsidiary math list. Math symbols have family and position numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing math material, conceptualize it as atoms with fields; assign mathcodes/families properly to obtain expected layout and spacing.
